sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Alpharetta, Georgia?
sections.html:
Alpharetta sellers choose between a full listing, a sale without an agent, or a cash purchase that closes on the seller's schedule. With a middle home value of $649,000 per the Census Bureau, the decision usually comes down to condition, timing and how much work you want to do before showing the house.

Alpharetta sits in northern Fulton County, about 26 miles north of downtown Atlanta. It was the town of Milton until 1858, when the city was chartered, and it served as the seat of Milton County until 1931, when that county merged into Fulton County during the Great Depression.

The city covers 26.9 square miles of land and borders Johns Creek to the southeast, Roswell to the south and west, Milton to the north and unincorporated Forsyth County to the northeast. The 2020 Census density was about 2,447 residents per square mile. The climate is humid subtropical and falls in USDA hardiness zone 7b, which affects what landscaping survives and how mature trees shade a lot.

  • Traditional listing: a good fit for a move-in ready house, where polish and staging can draw several offers.
  • Sale by owner: workable if you price from recent comparable sales and have a closing attorney lined up.
  • Cash sale as-is: useful for an inherited house, a property needing major updates, or a seller relocating on short notice.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Alpharetta homes and households?
sections.html:
Alpharetta is an owner-occupied, high-income city. The Census Bureau estimates 66,921 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 1.7 percent from the April 2020 base of 65,810.

Alpharetta city snapshot from Census QuickFacts (2020-2024 survey period unless noted)

Share of homes occupied by their owners65.1%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$649,000
Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage$2,950

Median household income (2024 dollars)$147,612

The same release shows 27.8 percent of residents are foreign-born and 32.8 percent speak a language other than English at home, so many households here come from outside the United States or speak another language at home.

sections.h2: Which employers and amenities draw buyers to Alpharetta?
sections.html:
Corporate offices are the main driver. The city's economic development figures, as of February 2026, list Fiserv at 2,087 employees, ADP at 2,074, MCI (Verizon) at 1,928 and Equifax at 1,722, followed by Jackson Healthcare, Morgan Stanley, UPS Supply Chain Solutions, Toyota Motor Credit and Ernst and Young. A house close to these offices can highlight a short commute in its listing.

Downtown Alpharetta, the 86-acre Avalon development that opened in 2014, and the Alpharetta City Center complex give the city walkable dining and shopping. North Point Mall is set for redevelopment. Outdoor amenities include the Big Creek Greenway and the Alpha Loop, a multi-use trail network now more than six miles long.

Alpharetta has no direct MARTA rail service, though several bus routes connect it to metro Atlanta.

Fulton County Schools serves the city, and Alpharetta High School serves most of Alpharetta, so the school zone is often the first question a family asks. Other high schools that draw from the surrounding area include Cambridge, Centennial, Chattahoochee, Johns Creek, Milton, Northview and Roswell.

Elementary schools listed for the city include Abbotts Hill, Alpharetta Elementary, Creek View, Dolvin, Lake Windward, Manning Oaks and New Prospect, and the public charter Amana Academy covers kindergarten through eighth grade. Higher education is also local: Perimeter College at Georgia State University, Gwinnett Technical College and Reinhardt University all have campuses in Alpharetta. Check the Fulton County Schools attendance lookup for the exact address before you advertise a school zone.

sections.h2: Is the house really inside Alpharetta city limits?
sections.html:
An Alpharetta mailing address does not always mean the property is in the city. The Halcyon mixed-use district, for example, carries an Alpharetta postal address but lies in Forsyth County, outside the city limits and outside Fulton County. Alpharetta's own ZIP codes are 30004, 30005, 30009 and 30022.

That detail affects who taxes the house. The City of Alpharetta levies its own property tax for city operations and voter-approved bonds, and it runs its own homestead exemption page, while Fulton County sets the assessment. A house with an Alpharetta address in another jurisdiction is taxed by different governments. Look at your tax bill or ask the Fulton County Board of Assessors to confirm which governments tax your parcel before you disclose costs to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do Fulton County assessments and appeals work for an Alpharetta seller?
sections.html:
Fulton County's Board of Assessors issues a notice of assessment each year for every property, and an owner who disagrees with the fair market value can appeal within 45 days of the date on the notice. The county says you can appeal only the assessed value and not the estimated tax, and that you lose the right to appeal if you miss the deadline printed on the notice.

  • File online, in person at one of five Fulton County locations, or by mail.
  • Pick one path when you file: a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on value, or a Hearing Officer, with fees possible for the last two.
  • Expect the appeal to take months, and pay any temporary bill while it is pending to avoid penalties.

North Fulton residents can use the customer service center on Roswell Road, which the county lists at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210. If a pending appeal is still open at closing, tell the closing attorney so the buyer sees the whole picture.

sections.h2: What city services and permits come up when you sell in Alpharetta?
sections.html:
The City of Alpharetta website groups its seller-relevant forms in one place. Its Apply menu lists a permitting portal, building construction permits, business licenses, homestead exemptions, and a form to establish or terminate trash service. Water and sewer bills are paid through Fulton County, so closing that account is a separate step from the city's trash account.

Short-term rentals have their own page under the city's Business section. If you plan to tell a buyer that the house can be rented by the night, ask the city's planning and zoning division for the current rules in writing first, since a rule change or a homeowner association restriction can end that plan. Work such as a deck, a finished basement or a new HVAC system should be checked against the permitting portal so open permits do not delay a closing.

sections.h2: What does Georgia require to transfer a deed after an Alpharetta sale?
sections.html:
Before a deed can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, Georgia's real estate transfer tax has to be paid. The Department of Revenue states the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100, with fractions counted as full units.

The seller is liable for the tax, though many contracts assign it to the buyer. The state's recording authority, the GSCCCA, provides the electronic PT-61 form that reports the sale. The Department of Revenue directs questions about taxability and exemptions to the Clerk of Superior Court in the county, which for Alpharetta means Fulton County.

faqs.q: How does Alpharetta's median home value compare with Albany and Athens?
faqs.a: Much higher. The Census Bureau lists Alpharetta's median owner-occupied home value at $649,000, compared with $124,300 in Albany and $299,200 in Athens-Clarke County for the same 2020-2024 period.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Fulton County assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is 45 days from the date of the Notice of Assessment. The date printed on your notice controls, and the appeal covers value only.

faqs.q: Does an Alpharetta mailing address mean my house is in the city?
faqs.a: Not always. Halcyon, for instance, uses an Alpharetta address but sits in Forsyth County outside city limits. Check your tax bill or ask the Fulton County Board of Assessors.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate transfer tax on an Alpharetta sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under Georgia's rule, and the contract may assign it to the buyer. The state rate is $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents for each additional $100.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Alpharetta house with open permits?
faqs.a: Ask the city's building permit staff through the permitting portal what is open on the address, and tell the buyer about any permit that has not been finished and approved.
